leftEvidence.title: “How long?” becomes petition, trust, and song

points.label: Prayer setting and claim
points.left: Repeated “how long” questions become petition and then trust and song without explaining the transition.
points.right: Slain witnesses cry “How long?” and receive robes and a command to rest rather than immediate judgment.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Repeated “how long” questions become petition and then trust and song without explaining the transition.
points.right: Slain witnesses cry “How long?” and receive robes and a command to rest rather than immediate judgment.

payload.posture: Psalm 13 and Revelation 6 address God with the same urgent question.

rightEvidence.title: The slain witnesses ask “How long?” and are told to rest

payload.tension: The psalm ends in trust and song; Revelation gives robes and rest while delaying the requested judgment.
payload.title: “How long?” before trust and before delay
